source_review.notes: Checked current Intel, AMD, Arm, RISC-V, Linux KVM, QEMU and Linux memory-management documentation for paging, nested translation, memory regions, invalidation, user-managed faults and same-page merging. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; architecture contracts, implementation mechanisms, abstract models and assurance claims remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked guest-virtual, guest-physical, host-physical, stage, permission, configured, resident, pinned, reclaimable, bandwidth, dirty-rate and generation notation.
Reviewed translation composition, permission intersection, pinned-capacity inequality and pre-copy recurrence.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates address owners, architectural permissions, host backing states and migration observations.

evidence: Executed three accesses through flat page-sized stage-one and stage-two mappings.
Confirmed one read resolves to HPA 0x28080, one write is denied at stage two and one write is denied at stage one; independently recomputed pre-copy rounds of 4.5 and 1.6875 GiB.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates one flat translation toy only; it implements no hardware walk, TLB, fault syndrome, memory attributes, concurrency or backing lifecycle.

evidence: Re-derived successful translation as monitor translation composed with guest translation and effective authority as permission-set intersection.
Checked the pinned-memory necessary bound, idealized pre-copy recurrence and generation-valid derived translation rule.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are subsystem reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of an ISA, MMU, host memory manager, VMM, IOMMU or migration protocol.

evidence: Reviewed walk faults, stage attribution, aliases, conflicting memory types, huge-page splits, tag reuse, host copy-on-write and secondary-TLB ordering.
Reviewed balloon races, double paging, deduplication, dirty-log clearing, DMA writes, post-copy duplicate faults, confidential conversion and teardown reuse.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Translation, fault, backing, invalidation, sharing, lifecycle, migration, device, pressure and confidentiality boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced GVA, GPA, HVA, HPA and IOVA ownership through stage-one, stage-two, host-MM and device paths.
Verified permission non-expansion, generation-aware invalidation, coherent region identity, lossless dirty tracking, one page owner and progress reserves.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats CPU translations, host backing, device mappings, dirty state and migration as coupled but separately owned memory state.

evidence: Reviewed isolation from GPA ownership through backing, composed permissions and revocation before reuse for CPU and device paths.
Constructed counterexamples for guest-physical-as-HPA, two-stage-as-two-accesses, TLB-flush-as-global-completion, unmap-as-DMA-stop and dirty-bitmap-read-as-race-free.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable guest-memory obligations, not a formal proof of a processor, hypervisor, host kernel, VMM, device, workload or migration system.

evidence: Audited uses of mapped, resident, pinned, reclaimable, permitted, invalidated, dirty, shared, private, migrated and confidential.
Confirmed architecture rules, kernel mechanisms, abstract capacity models, operational guidance, examples and assurance limits remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Configured memory is not labeled resident, guest physical is not labeled host physical, observed dirtiness is not labeled destination difference and confidential memory is not labeled universally inaccessible.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-084/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the translation toy.
Reviewed required page-table, processor, microcode, hypervisor, kernel, VMM, backend, IOMMU, NUMA, dirty-log, sharing, device and migration evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes three abstract mapping outcomes only; it provides no evidence for hardware translation, TLB coherence, page ownership, migration correctness, performance or security.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed guest memory as a composed address, permission, backing and lifecycle system spanning guest policy, monitor ownership, host memory and device access.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including memory slots, nested and shadow translation, A/D state, fault ownership, invalidation, huge pages, NUMA, overcommit, ballooning, KSM, dirty logs, migration, DMA and confidential pages. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from address domains and physical maps through translation, permissions, faults, invalidation, backing, pressure, dirty tracking, migration, devices and confidential memory, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, ISA or MMU architect, hypervisor or kernel maintainer, migration engineer, security reviewer, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
